desc: DONE: selected direct raw m1n1 for B0. The byte stream is exact 16-KiB-aligned m1n1.bin prefix, chosen.bootargs, gzip/XZ kernel, raw FDT, gzip/XZ initramfs, and >=4 zero bytes; raw entry is 0x800 and no outer container/Mach-O/SPTM path is used. Added strict host verifier with exact-member/hash, order/count, compression integrity, truncation/tail, entry/alignment, 64-MiB object policy, and expansion/runtime budgets; built and parsed a 21,728,804-byte in-memory fixture. Current local m1n1 has unapproved PCIe work and is explicitly not a B0 input. Result: done/2026-07-23-t6040-raw-boot-object-layout.md; verifier: scripts/t6040-raw-object-verify.py. No APFS, Boot Policy, enrollment, or rig access occurred. SIZE CEILING MEASURED 2026-07-25 (claude): the 64 MiB policy in this audit was an assumption; it is now measured-good. probe-graded-64M.bin (df1075b9, exactly 64.00 MiB = 4096 pages, self-describing stamps) enrolls, boots, and reads back with every sampled block through 63.05 MiB intact — iBoot loads the WHOLE 64 MiB object, so the ceiling is >=64 MiB and was not reached. IMPORTANT: the old '22.2 MB fails' data point is confounded (that object was non-page-aligned; see ticket 129) and must not be cited as a size limit. Page alignment to 16 KiB is the real constraint and is now enforced by scripts/t6040-build-raw-object.py. Evidence: done/2026-07-25-t6040-object-size-ceiling.md. CEILING 256 MiB MEASURED 2026-07-25 (claude): probe-graded-256M.bin (c7fcfa71, exactly 256 MiB = 16384 pages) enrolls, boots and reads back with every sampled block through 255.05 MiB intact — the whole object loads. No size ceiling has been found at any tested size (1.05 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 64 / 256 MiB all load fully); 16 KiB page alignment remains the only demonstrated constraint. Raise the builder's policy ceiling from the assumed 64 MiB to 256 MiB measured-good, and stop treating object size as a design constraint. The binding limit is now RAM for the unpacked root (~23 GiB available vs ~0.7-1 GB from a 256 MiB xz payload).
